quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry or upset, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid making eye contact with them.
Do not make hand gestures at them.

questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, keep your distance from them. Do not look at them or make gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move to another lane, or do whatever is safe to stay away from danger.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where they can safely cross. The lines may be horizontal, vertical, or both. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving does not increase your risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving distracts you and increases your chance of a crash.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before reaching the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell you to slow down. When a new speed limit is shown on this sign, the new speed starts right at the sign.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and rearview often to see if someone is tailgating you. If they are too close, slow down to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You are merging onto a busy freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and give the right-of-way to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before you merge to make sure you have room.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: When turning, reduce your speed so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and respond to unexpected situations.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired while driving, stop driving right away.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel hard to force your vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement slowly.
Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the wheel slowly to return to the pavement safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the wheel slowly to return to the pavement safely.
questions.explanation: Keep driving with the wheels off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. When you are going slow enough, turn the wheel to return to the pavement. Do not jerk the wheel hard to force your vehicle back on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead is now divided. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This speed sign shows the safest speed to use when exiting a highway. In this example, the safe exit speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: Highway signs that show hazardous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about possible hazards ahead. You must obey these signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can cause accidents.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Eating can slow alcohol absorption but cannot stop you from getting drunk if you drink too much.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other slippery conditions. Winter is hard and needs extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads.

questions.question: To stop hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Keep your tires at the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tire tread in good condition and inflate tires properly. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens most at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly to give vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know to move.
Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. Stopping before the sidewalk is required by law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. This sign tells you a lane is ending. Get ready for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Be alert for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing. Be careful and watch for people crossing.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. Low vehicles may drag or get caught on the tracks.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed. You may only pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times while driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them. Do not follow closely behind a large vehicle. The driver cannot see you there.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that their mirrors cannot see.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, and ambulances when they use a siren or horn and flashing red or blue lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only go when you are sure the road is clear.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones on highways. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols and warn that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, remove your foot from the gas pedal. Do not immediately brake. Gradually slow down, then gently brake and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.

questions.question: At night, how should you look to reduce headlight glare?

options.text: At the center of the road
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. The bright light can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: Drivers do not need to yield to pedestrians who are jaywalking or walking against the traffic light.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Pedestrians may cross against the light by mistake, so always be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which traffic light means: stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then go when the way is clear?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.
